title: Pocket Sundial with Fold-Flat Gnomon and Compass Seat
description: Palm-size 96 mm horizontal sundial: hour lines for 40 deg N latitude, a gnomon that folds flat on a hinge pin and stops plumb when raised, and a 20 mm recess for a stick-in button compass (not included).
use: Teaching tool and trail curiosity: set it level, align the 12 line north with a compass, read solar time. Fold the gnomon down to pack it flat.
material: PLA/PETG, 0.12-0.16 mm layers; hour lines are 0.7 mm deep grooves (paint-fill them). Pin: 3 mm PETG rod or filament cut to 33 mm.

problem_solved: Trail navigation gadgets are either bulky or need batteries. This one tells solar time and shows north when you add a button compass, packs flat in a pocket, and teaches how sundials work.
mechanism: Gnomon plate on a 3 mm pin between two ears; folds 90 deg onto the dial; a stop block touches the plate at plumb so it self-locates upright.
tolerances: Pin 1.5 mm radius in ears 1.6 (0.1 press) and gnomon bore 1.9 (0.4 free); folded plate floats 0.3 mm above the dial; stop gap 0.3 mm.
assembly: 1. Print dial (face up), gnomon (flat) and pin.
2. Lay the gnomon lug between the two ears and slide the pin through.
3. Press a 20 mm button compass into the recess.
4. Lift gnomon until it touches the stop.
fit_notes: Latitude is baked in (40 deg N; change `lat` in the source to regenerate for your location). Compass not included.
